body:
The gap is that the tool loop guard only read turns that had results. `exchanges`/`exchangeOf` in `internal/gateway/tool_loop.go` stop at a turn with no tool result, and `mayLoop` parsed only a body holding 8 tool results, so a conversation whose turns are the same call with nothing answering it was never read at all. That is the shape your 1088 entries describe: every reply a ~150-token tool call, the prompt growing by the call alone, no tool result ever added.

The branch reads that shape too. `toolLoopUnansweredOf` walks the request's own messages back from the newest and counts the calls asked in a row with no result after them, same name and arguments, call ids ignored. Eight in a row answer the turn here, in the agent's own protocol, with a notice that says the result never came back (nothing claims the call did not run), and the turn goes nowhere. The Routing view and the usage row are the existing `Tool loop stopped` / `tool loop:` rejection, so `/api/sessions` and Usage show it. A turn asking a different call, a reply that says something else, a result, or a word from the user starts the count again. No new setting and no new string: Settings › Models › Replies › *Stop looping replies* turns it off with the reply guard.

[fix/3615-loop-guard-does-not-cover](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3615-loop-guard-does-not-cover), commit 125a5e087ef882a6223dff6645589b0ee33cdbd6

Run: `TestToolLoopStuckWithoutResults` fails before the change on all eight protocol cases (Responses streamed and whole, Codex's own path, Chat streamed and whole, Anthropic streamed and whole, Gemini) with the vendor's reply reaching the agent, and passes after, the vendor asked 0 times; 7 turns go on. `TestToolLoopStuckNeedsTheSameCallAndNoWord` holds the progress cases. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/gateway/`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/gateway/` and `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/ -run 'TestToolLoop'` are clean. The full `internal/gateway` suite was run once and failed only in five tests that fail the same way on clean `upstream/main` (`TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged`, `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget`, `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` and `FuzzMarshalRaw`'s `\u2028` escaping, `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback`); a second full-suite run at the committed head was not completed.

This is a fork branch, ready to review, and not a claim on the issue. It does not add the per-session windowed cap or a refusal for the session, which you also floated: those need a new setting and per-session state, so that part is left to the maintainer.
